what_its_for: Prasugrel is a blood thinner that helps prevent dangerous blood clots from forming in your arteries. It is used to lower your risk of heart attack or stroke if you have had a recent heart attack or have been treated with a procedure to open blocked arteries (such as a stent placement). It works by stopping your platelets (tiny blood cells) from sticking together and forming harmful clots.
how_to_take: Take prasugrel by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. It is very important that you take this medication every day and do not skip doses. Do NOT stop taking prasugrel without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine. Stopping suddenly can greatly increase your risk of having a heart attack.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 60 mg taken one time (a loading dose). After that, the typical maintenance dose is 10 mg taken once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose to 5 mg once daily if you weigh less than 132 pounds (60 kg). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store prasugrel at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed and keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that could cause cuts or injuries that are hard to stop bleeding, such as contact sports or using sharp tools carelessly. Avoid taking aspirin in doses higher than your doctor recommends. Avoid other blood thinners, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other anti-inflammatory pain relievers unless your doctor approves. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can increase your risk of bleeding. Tell all of your doctors and your dentist that you take prasugrel before any surgery or dental procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual or uncontrolled bleeding (such as bleeding that won't stop from a cut), coughing or vomiting blood, blood in your urine (pink, red, or dark brown color), black or tarry stools, severe headache, dizziness, or weakness, vision changes, or signs of a stroke (sudden numbness, confusion, trouble speaking, or face drooping). Also call your doctor if you develop a fever, extreme tiredness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or purple or red spots under the skin, as these can be signs of a rare but serious blood condition.
when_it_works: Prasugrel starts working quickly — usually within 30 minutes of your first dose. However, it is meant to protect you over the long term, so it is important to keep taking it every day as prescribed. Most people take this medication for at least 12 months or longer, depending on their heart condition. Do not stop taking it just because you feel well.
special_populations: ELDERLY (75 years or older): Prasugrel is generally NOT recommended for patients 75 years or older unless your doctor decides the benefits outweigh the risks, because older adults have a higher risk of serious bleeding. LOW BODY WEIGHT: If you weigh less than 132 pounds (60 kg), your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose (5 mg per day) to reduce your bleeding risk. PREGNANCY & BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits must be carefully considered. HISTORY OF STROKE OR TIA: Prasugrel should NOT be used if you have ever had a stroke or a mini-stroke (TIA). Tell your doctor about your full medical history before starting this medication. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems, as this may affect whether prasugrel is right for you.
